domain_label: Study System — Planner: The Three-Layer Verification Loop & the Observed Failure Taxonomy
purpose: A method for the FACTORY build planner to run the mandatory three-layer verification loop on every build pass (builder ledger -> independent fresh-context audit vs code at a named HEAD SHA -> runtime self-check) so that 'reported complete' never substitutes for 'verified complete', and to apply the five documented incident rules (BKT silent revert, GitHub sync clobber, D-1 writeEdge bypass, D-3 TermLink gap, Slice 7 phantom-build) each to the layer that catches it — a build honesty discipline distinct from sysloops' runtime nightly loop.
assumptions: no observed run of a planner-orchestrated build is supplied as a labeled dataset; the five incidents are documented in the repo's own build history (PROTOCOL.md, SLICE_6_5.md, NEW_FEATURES_PLAN.md) and are cited [FACT-source] verbatim; the loop design around them is [ESTIMATE] design synthesis
the independent audit is a SEPARATE context (a second model / Codex), not the builder; the builder's own 'complete/verified' is never acceptance
'idempotent' and 'loop' here are BUILD-TIME senses (a duplicate-safe import re-run; the verification loop of a pass), not sysloops' runtime senses
acceptance is artifact-existence + behavior verified at a named HEAD SHA, never a ledger row or a design intention
exclusions: the runtime nightly-analysis loop, self-metrics scorecard, and runtime degraded-mode (owned by sysloops; planner's degraded-honest principle applies to BUILD honesty, not the nightly plan)
writing or fixing the app's code (the build agent does that under the governing specialist)
the internal design of any invariant or import the audit verifies (owned by the domain specialist; planner verifies it holds in code)
slice decomposition/sequencing (kb1) and owner-gate design / continuous-mode discipline (kb3)
inventing any exam-blueprint number, endpoint, price or clinical fact

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states that three independent audits each caught a gap a 'complete/verified' report missed, so the builder's claim is never acceptance

competency_questions.question: What are the three layers of the verification loop and why are all three needed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names builder ledger -> independent audit -> runtime self-check, mandatory and unskippable, with each catching a distinct failure class

competency_questions.question: What is the builder ledger and why is it not acceptance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: an append-only dated row (slice, result, per-check PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED-BY-GATE, gates awaiting owner) that the audit diffs against, but which is not itself acceptance

competency_questions.question: How does the independent audit work, and what does it catch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a fresh-context diff of the ledger claim against code at a named HEAD SHA; caught D-1, D-3 and the bulk-endpoint parity gap

competency_questions.question: Why does model/logic code need a runtime self-check?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a version marker + refuse-revert behavioral check, because layers 1-2 reduce but do not close the clobber window; catches the BKT revert and the Slice 7 phantom

competency_questions.question: What counts as acceptance, and what is graded FAIL?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: acceptance = artifact-exists-in-code AND behaves-as-specified at a named SHA; a reported-complete claim with no artifact is FAIL

competency_questions.question: What does the BKT silent-revert incident force?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: after any revert re-run the affected slice's behavioral self-checks; a model/logic revert re-runs its acceptance checks; caught by layer 3

competency_questions.question: What does the GitHub sync-clobber incident force?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: unsynced=unfinished; after every 'Synced N commits' event diff the last pass vs code and restore before advancing; docs pushed only between passes; caught by layer 2

competency_questions.question: How are the D-1 bypass and D-3 gap graded, and how is import idempotency proven?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a sole-write-path invariant is verified against code (D-1) and a recorded-complete-without-artifact is FAIL (D-3); idempotency proven by re-running the import with counts unchanged

competency_questions.question: Why is a slice with an off-repo runtime dependency not shipped?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the Slice 7 phantom (off-repo Worker) shows a slice whose runtime dependency is not in the repo is graded PARTIAL, not done; flag phantom deps as blockers; caught by layers 2+3

competency_questions.question: Why does a degraded-honest partial beat a phantom-complete?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: a valid partial with the gap named in the ledger is auditable and rebuildable; a phantom-complete hides the gap until production

competency_questions.question: How does planner's verification loop stay disjoint from sysloops' runtime loop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: loop/idempotent/router are used in build-time senses; runtime-loop-internal verification questions defer to sysloops

glossary.definition: the mandatory, unskippable loop planner runs on every pass: (1) builder ledger, (2) independent fresh-context audit vs code at a named HEAD SHA, (3) runtime self-check; each catches a distinct failure class and the builder's own claim is never acceptance [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md ledger-truth note]

layer 1 — an append-only dated PROGRESS row (slice, one-line result, each acceptance check PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED-BY-GATE, gates awaiting owner) that history is never rewritten over; the audit's diff input, not acceptance [FACT-source: PROTOCOL step 7]

layer 2 — a fresh-context pass (a second model/Codex, not the builder) diffing the ledger claim against actual code at a named HEAD SHA; caught D-1, D-3 and the bulk-endpoint parity gap [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md G0 at origin/main f43cc69]

layer 3 — a version marker + behavioral check on model/logic code that refuses a reverted model, needed because layers 1-2 reduce but do not close the clobber window [FACT-source: PROTOCOL sync-discipline rule 4]

the binding principle that a builder's 'complete/verified' is never acceptance; acceptance is independent verification of artifact-existence + behavior, because three separate audits each overturned a 'complete' report [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md ledger-truth note]

a version-history revert of a bad visual change silently rolled back the BKT model fix; forces: after any revert re-run behavioral self-checks, a model/logic revert re-runs acceptance; caught by layer 3 [FACT-source: PROTOCOL]

two-way sync clobbered built work twice (bkt_evidence; Slice 6.5 Pass 1 via a 4-commit doc-sync); forces: unsynced=unfinished, diff-and-restore after every 'Synced N commits', docs pushed only between passes; caught by layer 2 [FACT-source: PROTOCOL sync discipline]

kgImport created edges via ConceptEdge.create, bypassing the writeEdge sole-write-path invariant while reporting complete; forces: invariants are code-verified acceptance items, import idempotency proven by re-run with counts unchanged; caught by layer 2 [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md G0 D-1]

the TermLink entity + linkTerms function were never built though Step 1 was recorded complete; forces: recorded-complete-without-artifact = FAIL, acceptance is artifact-existence + behavior not the ledger row; caught by layer 2 [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md G0 D-3]

the media build was reported but delegated to an off-repo home-lab Worker absent from the repo (w_optimized/VoiceQueue dead ends), graded PARTIAL; forces: a slice whose runtime dependency is not in the repo is not shipped, flag phantom deps as blockers; caught by layers 2+3 [FACT-source: NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §5]

a duplicate-safe re-run of an import/build, proven by re-running the same import and confirming unchanged counts (duplicates rejected, dangling-drop preserved); planner verifies it, the owning specialist designs it — distinct from sysloops' runtime nightly-re-run idempotency [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md D-1 acceptance]

a valid partial with the gap named in the ledger always beats a report of complete that isn't; the build-time analog of sysloops' 'a valid degraded plan beats a rich broken one' [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md D-2/D-3; NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §5]

nodes.definition: Frame the layer: this KB owns planner's VERIFICATION discipline — the rule that 'reported complete' never substitutes for 'verified complete'. It exists because an independent audit has THREE times found a gap that a 'complete/verified' builder report missed (silent BKT revert; bulk-endpoint parity; the D-1/D-3 audit) [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md ledger-truth note]. planner runs a three-layer loop (builder ledger -> independent fresh-context audit -> runtime self-check) on every pass; the builder's own claim is never acceptance [ESTIMATE — design synthesis grounded in the documented incidents].

the three-independent-audits track record that motivates the loop

excluded: the five-incident taxonomy details (each has its own node)

pros.claim: Making reported!=verified the frame forces the loop onto every pass, not just suspicious ones
pros.example: the same 'complete/verified' phrasing preceded all three caught gaps, so it earns zero trust by itself

cons.claim: A three-layer loop on every pass is real overhead when most passes are honest
cons.example: a trivially-correct pass still pays for a fresh-context audit

nodes.definition: The mandatory, never-skipped loop of three layers: (1) BUILDER LEDGER — the build agent appends a dated row (slice, one-line result, each acceptance check PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED-BY-GATE, gates awaiting owner); (2) INDEPENDENT AUDIT — a fresh-context pass diffs the ledger's claim against the actual code at a named HEAD SHA; (3) RUNTIME SELF-CHECK — model/logic code carries a version marker + a behavioral check that refuses a reverted model [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md 'builder ledger -> independent audit -> runtime check stays mandatory'; PROTOCOL sync-discipline rule 4]. Layers 1-2 reduce but do not close the clobber window, which is why layer 3 exists.

included: the three named layers and their order
the mandatory/unskippable status
the reason layer 3 exists (layers 1-2 do not close the window)
excluded: each layer's own detailed node (BUILDER_LEDGER / INDEPENDENT_AUDIT / RUNTIME_SELF_CHECK)

pros.claim: Three independent layers catch different failure classes; no single layer would catch all five incidents
pros.example: the audit catches D-1/D-3/parity; the runtime check catches the silent BKT revert; the ledger anchors both

cons.claim: Three layers cost a ledger write, a fresh-context pass and a code marker on every model/logic change
cons.example: a pure-cosmetic pass still needs the ledger row even if the audit is light

the layers are not truly independent (the builder audits itself)
acceptance_tests: all three layers are specified as mandatory

The ledger is the record (not chat); it is the input the independent audit diffs against, but it is NOT itself acceptance.

This is distinct from sysloops' runtime idempotency (a nightly re-run reproducing the same DB state), which planner does not design.

priority_rationale: The reported!=verified frame and the three-layer loop come first because they are the reason the KB exists and everything else is a layer or an incident under them. The three layers (ledger, audit, runtime self-check) precede the taxonomy because each incident is classified by the layer that catches it. The ledger-not-acceptance and artifact-existence principles sit between the layers and the incidents because they are the general rules the incidents instantiate. The five incidents are ordered by the layer that catches them (revert->runtime; sync/D-1/D-3->audit; phantom->audit+runtime). Idempotency-as-acceptance and degraded-honest come near the end as the two positive acceptance/grading principles distilled from the incidents, and the sysloops fence closes the KB by disambiguating the shared loop/idempotent/router vocabulary.
